_comment: One source for what the public pages say about the app. The landing page is rendered from it on the server and the app's 'new version' notice reads it, so a change here (made in the same pull request as the feature) shows up everywhere. Add a whatsNew entry, newest first, for every change users will notice. The stages must match the Journey's stage picker (a test checks). The tour is the feature slides: the landing page plays all of them, and a new account's dashboard plays the ones with an action, with a button for each. Each stage card opens in its `view` (2d or 3d), with a switch for the other.

stages.name: Football
stages.line: Dribble past rival players and score at the goal.

stages.name: Space
stages.line: Fly up beside asteroids and alien saucers and blast them.

stages.name: Castle
stages.line: A knight swings at giant frogs and black knights on the way to the dragon.

stages.name: Construction
stages.line: Watch the building go up phase by phase as tasks are done.

stages.name: Sprint Track
stages.line: Run your lane in an Olympic stadium, clear the hurdles and break the tape. Racing friends? Everyone gets a lane.

tour.name: Plan with the assistant
tour.title: Tell it your goal
tour.text: Type or say what you want to finish. The assistant drafts a phased plan with dated tasks, and nothing changes until you approve it.

tour.name: Start my day
tour.title: Your day, planned to the minute
tour.text: A good-morning notification opens today's plan as a timetable. Then a Pacer keeps to your times while you work: finish tasks to stay on plan or get ahead.

tour.name: Blockers you can see
tour.title: Name what's in the way
tour.text: Tick each blocker off as it's sorted. Tasks wait for the ones before them, and nothing is marked done while a blocker is still pending.

tour.name: Your why
tour.title: Remember why you started
tour.text: Your reason, your mentor, quotes from the sources you choose and your music, found in a two minute chat and shown when you'd give up.

tour.name: Rewards
tour.title: Rewards from people who believe in you
tour.text: Send a private link and a parent, boss, coach or friend can promise a reward for finishing. It's marked earned the moment you do.

tour.name: Streaks and check-ins
tour.title: Keep the streak alive
tour.text: A daily streak, alarm style reminders, a morning list of what's due and a weekly note on what's on track and what's stalled.

tour.name: Plan together
tour.title: Bring your people in
tour.text: Invite viewers, commenters or editors. Comments with @mentions and a chat per goal with photos and files. Private goals stay private.

tour.name: Play your plan
tour.title: Your plan, as a game
tour.text: Your character walks your road in Football, Space, Castle or Construction, in 2D or 3D, clearing the blockers you name. The game layer is there when you want it.

whatsNew.title: The bell keeps up with your team and rewards
whatsNew.text: Notifications now tell you when a teammate is stuck and asks for help, when someone offers to help you, when a step is sent back or signed off, when steps are waiting for your sign-off, about cheers and finishes, and when a reward is pledged, earned, released or comes with a message. The important ones also arrive as a push, where you've turned push on.

whatsNew.title: Ask for help on a blocker
whatsNew.text: Stuck on a blocker in a race, group or shared goal? Tap Ask for help on it and say what's in the way. It goes in the chat, the leader is told, and teammates can answer with I can help. Clear the blocker and the chat says you got past it, and who helped.

whatsNew.title: Rewards: held gifts, release and messages
whatsNew.text: Whoever pledges a reward can now hold the gift in Waypoint (a ticket, voucher or booking code, a link and a note), hidden until you've earned it. When you finish, they check your steps and release it, and the gift appears on your goal. For cash, tell them how you'd like it sent (only they see it); Waypoint never handles the money. You and they also get your own message thread.

whatsNew.title: Team-ups in the planner
whatsNew.text: Steps from a race or group now carry a Squad, Class, Team or Race chip on Kanban and Gantt, and a step that doesn't count yet says so: needs proof, waiting for the coach, or sent back, with Add proof one tap away. The Gantt draws a chequered finish line at the team's finish date, and if you lead a group it shows one row per person, filled as far as they've got, with the steps waiting for your sign-off.

whatsNew.title: Proof and sign-off
whatsNew.text: No more ticking everything to win. When you team up, choose how steps are checked: trust everyone, a photo or a few words for each step, or (in a group) the coach, teacher or leader signs each step off. Proof goes in the chat, the leader can approve steps one at a time or all at once, or send one back with a note, and a burst of steps ticked inside a minute is pointed out in a race's chat.

whatsNew.title: Look around and zoom in 3D
whatsNew.text: On every 3D stage, drag (or swipe sideways) to look around or behind your character, and zoom with the scroll wheel, a pinch or the plus and minus buttons. The follow cam drifts back behind you after a moment, and Recentre puts the overview back.

whatsNew.title: Chat and cheers for races and groups
whatsNew.text: Every race and group now has its own chat, in the Chats inbox and on the race strip. Waypoint posts when someone joins, gets halfway or finishes, and a coach's reminder lands there too. Tap someone's name to cheer them on: the emoji floats up over their Journey.

whatsNew.title: A proper welcome on an empty dashboard
whatsNew.text: Before your first goal, the dashboard now shows three ways in: plan it with the assistant, start from a template or join a team with a code. Below them are the five Journey stages, so you can pick where your goal plays. A stray empty circle on the dashboard is gone too.

whatsNew.title: New stage: the Sprint Track
whatsNew.text: Run your lane in an Olympic stadium, in 2D or 3D. Tasks are split boards by the track, blockers are hurdles you jump, and finishing breaks the tape for a personal best. Racing friends? Everyone gets their own lane, and the big screen shows who is leading.

whatsNew.title: Clear finished races and groups from Teams
whatsNew.text: Once a race or group is over for you, clear it off your Teams list, one at a time or all at once with Clear finished. Only your list changes: everyone else still sees it on their scoreboard, and Undo brings it back.

whatsNew.title: Project picker fixed on phones
whatsNew.text: With more than seven projects, opening the project picker on a phone brought up the keyboard, which closed the picker straight away. It now opens as a sheet and stays open: tap the search box when you want it.

whatsNew.title: No more duplicate goal when you team up
whatsNew.text: Setting up a race or a group from one of your goals no longer copies it for you. You take part on the goal you already have, and only the people who join get their own copy. A race from a goal with steps already ticked still gives you a fresh copy, so everyone starts level.

whatsNew.title: Team up: for coaches, trainers, teachers and managers
whatsNew.text: Race a friend is now Team up. Lead a group comes first: say whether you are a coach, trainer, teacher or manager, and your squad, clients, class or team each get their own copy of the goal while you watch who is on track. Racing friends is still there as the second choice, and Challenges is now called Teams.

whatsNew.title: Fits tablets and small laptops
whatsNew.text: Toolbars, the project header and the task filters wrap instead of running off the side. Kanban columns stay readable and scroll, and the Journey puts its task list under the game when the screen is narrow. The pale haze down the right edge and an empty box above the Journey are gone.

whatsNew.title: Gold, silver and bronze cups on the scoreboard
whatsNew.text: The race report is now the Scoreboard. First, second and third get gold, silver and bronze cups on name tags, the podium and the table. The Close button on the finish summary works again.

whatsNew.title: 1st, 2nd, 3rd and a race report
whatsNew.text: Races now give finishing places with medals on everyone's name tag, your place when you finish, and a race report with a podium, everyone's times and who owes the stake.

whatsNew.title: Challenges for a class or team
whatsNew.text: Teachers and team leads can set one goal for everyone, share a 6-character code, and watch the class progress together, with names, first names or animal names. Nudge anyone who's behind with one tap.

whatsNew.title: Races in the 3D worlds too
whatsNew.text: Racing a friend? Switch the Journey to 3D and they're there: footballers, knights, builders or rockets in their own colour, with their name floating over them.

whatsNew.title: Race a friend to the finish
whatsNew.text: Turn any goal into a race: pick a finish date and what's riding on it, and send the link. Everyone gets their own copy, and on the Journey you all run the same road with your names over your heads.

whatsNew.title: Today's road from the focus timer
whatsNew.text: Tap the map on the focus timer to open today's road in full view, from any page and on your phone too.

whatsNew.title: Report a problem from inside the app
whatsNew.text: Something not right, or an idea? Tap Report a problem in the menu and tell us. We see which page you were on, so a sentence is enough, and we reply by email.

whatsNew.title: Opens faster on your phone
whatsNew.text: Waypoint now loads about half as much on your first visit and far less after that, so it opens quicker on mobile data.

whatsNew.title: Plan your first day in three steps
whatsNew.text: New to Waypoint? Name your goal, write the first three things to do, and see today laid out with times. You land on your own day, ready to start the first task.

whatsNew.title: Confirm your email
whatsNew.text: New accounts made with an email address now get a link to confirm it, so password resets and invites always reach the right person. You can use Waypoint straight away while you wait.

whatsNew.title: Less floating on the screen
whatsNew.text: The focus timer and the music player no longer stack up over the page. While the timer is open, your music keeps playing with its controls in the timer, and the timer stays small on your phone. On the dashboard, today comes first.

whatsNew.title: Tidier on your phone
whatsNew.text: Spacing, padding and text fixes across the app on small screens. Nothing scrolls sideways any more, task cards breathe, and buttons stay on one line.

whatsNew.title: Watch from a play icon, not a pop-up
whatsNew.text: Finish a task on today's plan or clear one of its blockers and a small play icon now sits beside it, instead of a message covering the screen. Press it whenever you like to watch it happen on today's road.

whatsNew.title: Pick how long to keep working
whatsNew.text: When today's plan is done, keep working for 15, 25, 45 or 60 minutes instead of a fixed 25. Waypoint remembers the length you picked last time.

whatsNew.title: Plan done? Keep going or close
whatsNew.text: Finish the last task on today's plan and the focus timer now asks what's next: plan more tasks, keep going with 25 minutes of focus time, or close it. Ticking a task off anywhere stops its timer too, and your music stays to hand.

whatsNew.title: Tasks that open the right app
whatsNew.text: Give a task an action (email, WhatsApp, call, text, meeting, directions, or booking a table, flight, taxi or hotel) and when its time comes, one tap opens Gmail, Outlook, WhatsApp, your phone, your calendar or Google Maps with everything filled in. Come back, tap Done, and it's ticked off. Find it in a task's Do it box, on today's road and on the focus timer.

whatsNew.title: Set your start time your way
whatsNew.text: Start my day now has a proper start-time picker: nudge it 15 minutes either way, pick from a list, type any custom time, or tap Now to start this minute. Switch between 12-hour (9:30 am) and 24-hour (09:30) times, and set any custom length for a task.

whatsNew.title: Turn the assistant's voice off
whatsNew.text: Prefer it quiet? Settings, Appearance, Assistant's voice now has an on and off switch. Off, the assistant won't speak on its own; tap a Listen button whenever you do want something read out.

whatsNew.title: Tick tasks off on today's road
whatsNew.text: The circle beside each stop on today's road is now a tick box: tick it to finish that task right there and watch your character walk on. Blockers still in the way? It shows you which, so you can clear them first.

whatsNew.title: Replay your day
whatsNew.text: Replay my day, in the Game view of today's road, plays your whole day back from the start: every blocker you knocked out and every task you finished, in the order they happened. Finish a task anywhere, even by dragging it to Completed, and you can Watch your character reach its stop. Ticked blockers now stay on cards and table rows, crossed out.

whatsNew.title: Clearer messages when a task is not ready yet
whatsNew.text: Try to finish a task that still has blockers and you now get a proper card instead of a red error: it lists what's in the way with a tick box for each, so you can clear them there and then and tap Mark as done. A task waiting on another one shows which, with a button to open it.

whatsNew.title: Drag and stretch Gantt bars, on your phone too
whatsNew.text: Drag a bar on the Gantt chart to move a task, or pull either end to change its start or due date. It snaps to whole days and shows the new dates as you go, and Undo is one tap away. On a phone or tablet, press and hold a bar for a moment, then drag. The Key button no longer slips off the edge of smaller phones.

whatsNew.title: Every Gantt column on your phone, and music links that just work
whatsNew.text: On a phone the Gantt chart now keeps status, start, due and duration: the task name stays put while you swipe across to them or on to the timeline, which opens on today. And paste a YouTube playlist, a Spotify link or any other music link into Add music and it plays straight away, even without the https:// in front.

whatsNew.title: How today went, and progress over time
whatsNew.text: When your planned day is over, How today went shows you against the Pacer as two lines across the day, when each task was finished against its slot, and what's left, which you can move to tomorrow's plan in one tap. Project reports now chart progress over time too: what you actually got done against what the plan expected, day by day.

whatsNew.title: One project picker that follows you
whatsNew.text: Pick a project on the Planner and the Calendar shows the same one, and Waypoint remembers it next time. The Journey always opens on a real project instead of an empty scene, and the picker itself is new: each project with its icon and colour, its sub-folders indented beneath it, and projects shared with you in their own section. The planner keys are laid out more cleanly too.

whatsNew.title: Watch the knockout
whatsNew.text: Ticked off a blocker on one of today's tasks from the task panel or the board? Tap Watch and today's road opens in the game, where your character knocks that blocker out in front of you, in 2D or 3D.

whatsNew.title: Knock blockers out on today's road
whatsNew.text: In the Game view of today's road, each stop now lists its blockers with a tick box. Tick one when it clears and watch your character knock it out in the world, in 2D or 3D.

whatsNew.title: Clear the last blocker, start the task
whatsNew.text: Blockers can be ticked off whenever they clear, even before you've started the task. Tick the last one on a task you haven't begun and Waypoint asks if you'd like to start it now: one tap and it's In Progress.

whatsNew.title: Play today's road as a game
whatsNew.text: Full view on today's road now has a Game mode. Your day becomes a Journey world, one stop per task, with you and the Pacer racing along it. Pick the world and switch between 2D and 3D right there; the list of today's stops sits underneath. Prefer it plain? Road mode is one tap away, and Waypoint remembers which you chose.

whatsNew.title: Race the Pacer through your day
whatsNew.text: Once you start your day, the focus timer shows today's road: a stop for each task, you moving as you finish them, and a Pacer keeping to the times you planned, like a pacer in a race. It tells you if you're ahead of or behind plan, the same strip sits on your dashboard, and Full view lays out the whole day. Music now lives on the timer too: pause, skip, or search and add a song without leaving your work.

whatsNew.title: A key for the planner, and a proper sign-in page
whatsNew.text: Tap Key on the Gantt chart, the board or the calendar to see what every colour, line and badge means. Signing in now has its own page, with what Waypoint does beside the form.

whatsNew.title: A morning that gets you going
whatsNew.text: Start my day now lays out today as a timetable with a time and a length for each task, asks what's in your way, offers a song, and shows today's quote for a moment before your first task starts. Set a wake-up time in Settings and a good-morning notification opens it for you. The dashboard is lighter too: just your plan and one button.

whatsNew.title: A guided start for new accounts
whatsNew.text: Until you finish your first task, the This week card on your dashboard plays short slides of what Waypoint can do, each with a button to try it. The same slides now play on the home page.

whatsNew.title: Simpler, with less to learn
whatsNew.text: One assistant does the planning everywhere, new accounts start with the plan and keep the game for when you want it, and four Journey worlds remain: Football, Space, Castle and Construction. Fewer extras means the parts you use every day are easier to find.

whatsNew.title: A dashboard that says each thing once
whatsNew.text: Today and your focus list are one card now, your week and your Journey sit beside it, and no task shows up twice. A different quote greets you each day, only from the sources you picked.

whatsNew.title: A team chat that's quicker to use
whatsNew.text: One + button for photos, files or emailing the team. Paste or drop a photo in, see it before you send, and write as much as you need: the box grows with you.

whatsNew.title: Bring in your Spotify and YouTube playlists
whatsNew.text: Connect your account and your own playlists show up in Your why, one tap to add. Search finds songs on Spotify and YouTube together, and pasted links get their real names.

whatsNew.title: Rewards from people who believe in you
whatsNew.text: Send a private link and a parent, boss, coach or friend can promise a reward for finishing your goal: cash, or anything else. It's marked earned the moment you finish.

whatsNew.title: Start my day sorts your day for you
whatsNew.text: One tap picks today's tasks, moves late ones to today and starts the first with your music. Finish one and it hands you the next.

whatsNew.title: A calmer Your why
whatsNew.text: See your why, your mentor, today's quote and your music at a glance, then change one thing at a time. It saves as you go.

whatsNew.title: A real moment when you finish a goal
whatsNew.text: Finishing a goal now gets the celebration it deserves: what you did (tasks, blockers beaten, how many days, how early you finished), a reminder of the why you gave, and a picture to share. Then plan what is next with the assistant, or open the report.

whatsNew.title: Find your why in a two-minute chat
whatsNew.text: No more forms: Your why is now a short conversation with your coach. Talk or type, and it fills in your reason, who you are becoming, your mentor, your words and your music for you to check and save. You choose where your words come from (the Bible, the Quran, books and speeches, or none), and you are only ever shown quotes from what you chose.

whatsNew.title: A personal assistant that runs your day with you
whatsNew.text: Each morning the assistant briefs you: what is late, what is due, your streak and a line from your why, read aloud if you like. Start my day begins a focus session on the first thing with your music on, and checks in when the time is up. Ask it anything about your plans, or tell it what to do: open a project, focus on a task for 25 minutes, remind me at 6, mark it done, add a task. Changes to your plans still wait for your tap. Press J anywhere to talk to it.

whatsNew.title: Your music, playing inside Waypoint
whatsNew.text: Save your playlists like in a music app (focus, workout, worship) from Spotify, YouTube, Apple Music, SoundCloud or Deezer. They play right inside Waypoint and keep going while you work and play your Journey, until you stop them. Skip between playlists, minimise the player, or just ask the assistant: play my workout playlist.

whatsNew.title: Your why: what keeps you going
whatsNew.text: Tell Waypoint why your goal matters, who you are becoming, who you look up to and their routine, the words that move you (your own, or a starter shelf of Bible, Quran and book quotes, each with its source) and your focus playlist. It brings them back when you are most likely to give up: when an alarm rings, when a task is stuck, on your dashboard each morning, in phone nudges and in the assistant's coaching.

whatsNew.title: A friendlier New project window
whatsNew.text: Start a project three ways: blank, from a ready-made template, or by describing your goal in a sentence for the assistant to plan. Pick an icon and colour with a tap, choose the area of life, and invite people if you like. New projects open straight away, ready for the first task.

whatsNew.title: Your week, playing on the dashboard
whatsNew.text: Open the app and your week plays as a short story right on the dashboard: tasks finished, your best day, blockers beaten, your streak, the project that moved most and what's coming up. Hover to pause, tap to skip, or open it full screen to share. The app also has a cleaner look, with one matching set of line icons in place of emoji.

whatsNew.title: Board-ready reports with photos
whatsNew.text: A new portfolio report puts all your projects, or the ones you pick, on one page for a board or team meeting: overall progress, which projects are behind, what needs a decision, what's coming up and recent wins, as a PDF or printout. And any project report can now include photos and files of progress or blockers, with captions, right inside the PDF and share link. The dashboard is simpler too: one Your focus list puts what's late or blocked first, with the reason, then what's due next.

whatsNew.title: Quicker tasks and a smarter dashboard
whatsNew.text: The task window leads with what matters and tucks repeat, target and cost into More options; status and priority are one tap. The task panel shows how long is left (or how late it is) and has a Start / Mark done button that tells you when a blocker is in the way. And the dashboard's Needs your attention lists what's overdue, blocked, due today or waiting, with Done and Remind right there.

whatsNew.title: Clear privacy and terms
whatsNew.text: Our Privacy Policy and Terms are rewritten in plain English for UK law: exactly what we collect and why, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and your rights. Deleting your account now also removes your usage history, and old usage records are cleared automatically after 13 months.

whatsNew.title: Microsoft accounts and OneDrive
whatsNew.text: Sign in with any Microsoft account (Outlook, Hotmail, work or school) as well as Google, and back up to OneDrive alongside Google Drive. The Gantt chart now shows its timeline properly on a phone held sideways too.

whatsNew.title: A tidier Settings
whatsNew.text: Settings now opens one section at a time: Profile, Notifications, Appearance, Connected apps, Data and Trash, and Security. Your profile shows who you are at a glance, and Trash groups everything by project, so a deleted project and all its tasks come back with one tap.

whatsNew.title: Focus mode, quicker status and honest progress
whatsNew.text: Focus mode in Settings hides XP, quests and trophies for serious goals. On the Gantt chart, status is a chip you tap to change. Progress now weighs each task by how long it takes, so a three-week task counts for more than a one-hour one. And the website has a playable demo, no sign-up needed.

whatsNew.title: Task alarms and a Blocked list
whatsNew.text: Set a reminder on any task and Waypoint rings like an alarm at that time: a full-screen alarm with sound in the app, and an alert that stays on your phone screen with Start and Snooze buttons, ringing again every few minutes until you respond. Actions now has a Blocked section showing exactly what is in each task's way.

whatsNew.title: A cleaner Kanban and a phone-friendly Gantt
whatsNew.text: Kanban cards have a fresh look with a Move menu that works by touch, and on phones the columns swipe side by side. The Gantt chart opens on today, keeps task names readable on a phone and shows status as a dot. Calendar now has its own tab in the phone bar.

whatsNew.title: A new assistant panel
whatsNew.text: The assistant now opens as a side panel next to your work, with a welcome card of one-tap starters, clearer chat bubbles, a typing indicator, and suggested changes you can tick and apply in one tap. On phones it fills the screen.

whatsNew.title: Smoother Journey in every world
whatsNew.text: The 3D camera now keeps your character in view when you beat a blocker and finish the task straight after, task names read in full, the scene fills its frame, and levelling up mid-game shows a banner instead of covering the action.

whatsNew.title: Two-step sign-in
whatsNew.text: Protect your account with a code from an authenticator app, like Google Authenticator or 1Password, on top of your password. Turn it on in Settings, with recovery codes in case you lose your phone.

whatsNew.title: Invite anyone, even before they join
whatsNew.text: Invite people while creating a project, and invite anyone by email: people without an account get an email to join, and the project is waiting for them the moment they sign up.

whatsNew.title: A fresh new look
whatsNew.text: A calmer, clearer design across the app and website: a focus card for your main goal with a Play button straight into its Journey, today's quests, your next tasks to tick off from the home screen, a tab bar on phones, and the game's streak and level pills always in view.

whatsNew.title: The game levels up: sounds, ranks and daily quests
whatsNew.text: Sounds and phone buzzes when you finish a task or beat a blocker, ranks from Rookie to Mythic with a level-up moment, three new quests every day for bonus XP, XP for beating blockers and finishing early, and 21 achievements to collect.

whatsNew.title: Progress reports you can share
whatsNew.text: Any project or goal now has a progress report: on track or behind, a forecast finish date, every phase, a timeline, what's done, what's next and what's in the way. Download it as a PDF, print it, email it, or share a live read-only link you can turn off at any time.

whatsNew.title: A command palette and your week in review
whatsNew.text: Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K) or tap ⌘ to jump anywhere, run any action, or type a task and add it in one go ("call the bank tomorrow"). And tap 🎬 My week for a Wrapped-style story of your last seven days that you can share.

whatsNew.title: Templates, Undo and your tasks in your calendar
whatsNew.text: Start a project from one of six ready-made plans, undo a delete straight from the toast, and subscribe to your due dates in Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar.

whatsNew.title: Faster, safer and easier to use
whatsNew.text: Pages load about four times lighter, password reset emails a link, sign-in is better protected, calendar weeks start on Monday in the UK, and there are keyboard shortcuts: / to search, n for a new task, a for the assistant.

whatsNew.title: Tasks unlock the moment you finish what they wait on
whatsNew.text: Tick off a predecessor and the tasks waiting on it open up straight away.

whatsNew.title: The assistant handles dependencies and targets
whatsNew.text: Ask it to make one task wait on another, or to set a target such as "write 20 pages", and approve the change.

whatsNew.title: A listening assistant with saved chats
whatsNew.text: A Shazam-style listening light, chat history you can come back to, and Ask AI on every project and task. Works with AirPods.

whatsNew.title: Product Launch stage
whatsNew.text: Take an idea from the lab to a launch stage full of happy customers, in 2D or 3D.

whatsNew.title: Blockers you fight in person
whatsNew.text: Name what's in your way and it appears on the Journey. Your character stays and deals with each one as you tick it off.

whatsNew.title: Task dependencies
whatsNew.text: Make a task wait for another to finish, shown with arrows on the Gantt chart.
